G, sec. 7343(b), verbatim: 'None of the funds authorized to be appropriated or otherwise made available by this division may be obligated or expended in support of any activity involving unidentified anomalous phenomena protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitation unless the Director of National Intelligence has provided the details of the activity to the appropriate committees of Congress and congressional leadership, including for any activities described in a report released by the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office in fiscal year 2024.' Text at 137 Stat. 1063-1064.

Sec. 7343(a)(1) defines 'appropriate committees of Congress' as SSCI, SASC and Senate Appropriations, and HPSCI, HASC and House Appropriations; (a)(2) adds the four congressional leaders. Sec. 7343(c) applies the same IR&D indirect-cost bar on the intelligence side.

Sections 1687 and 7343 are deliberately mirrored across the DoD/IC seam identified in 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(2)(B) and ICD 906 C.3 -- one addressed to the Secretary of Defense and binding this Act's funds, the other to the DNI and binding this division's funds. Together they attempt to cover both sides of the jurisdictional gap that the SAP reporting statutes leave open. Neither reaches money appropriated in other Acts or in prior years. Reasoning stated.

desc: Division G of Public Law 118-31 is the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, and its section 7343 mirrors section 1687 on the intelligence side with a different addressee and a wider committee list. Subsection (b): 'None of the funds authorized to be appropriated or otherwise made available by this division may be obligated or expended in support of any activity involving unidentified anomalous phenomena protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitation unless the Director of National Intelligence has provided the details of the activity to the appropriate committees of Congress and congressional leadership, including for any activities described in a report released by the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office in fiscal year 2024.' Its 'appropriate committees of Congress' are the Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on Appropriations of the House - six committees, plus the four congressional leaders. Subsection (c) carries the same independent research and development prohibition. Read together, sections 1687 and 7343 mean that as of 22 December 2023 both the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence are under a statutory funding prohibition for unreported UAP special access activity, and both prohibitions run to a combined audience far wider than the 10 U.S.C. 119(e) waiver group. Congress did not repeal the waiver; it built a subject-matter carve-out around it.

dossier.narrative:
The pairing is the point. Section 1687 addresses the Secretary of Defense and binds funds authorised by the NDAA; section 7343 addresses the Director of National Intelligence and binds funds authorised by the intelligence division. Read against 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(2)(B), which excludes the Department of Defense, the NNSA and IC agencies from the general SAP-reporting statute and routes each to its own regime, the pair looks less like duplication and more like Congress closing both sides of a seam it had itself created.

Neither text cites the other, and 3348 makes no reference to 7343. That was checked directly against the statutory text on 22 August 2026 rather than assumed, which is why the structural edges from this node are graded Tier 3.

dossier.whatItIs: Section 7343 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, enacted as division G of Pub. L. 118-31, 137 Stat. 1064, titled 'Funding Limitations Relating to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena'. Subsection (b) bars obligation or expenditure of funds authorised by that division 'in support of any activity involving unidentified anomalous phenomena protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitation' that has not been reported to Congress. Subsection (c) makes UAP-related independent research and development unallowable as an indirect expense. Subsection (a)(1) defines 'appropriate committees of Congress' as SSCI, SASC and Senate Appropriations, plus HPSCI, HASC and House Appropriations; (a)(2) adds the four congressional leaders.
dossier.whyImplicated:
7343 is the intelligence-community half of a matched pair. NDAA sec. 1687 imposes the same two limitations on defence funds through the Secretary of Defense; 7343 imposes them on intelligence funds through the Director of National Intelligence. Congress wrote the prohibition twice because the money and the authority run through two different chains, and a limitation binding only one of them would leave the other open. That is a legislative judgement about where UAP work could be hidden, expressed in enacted law rather than in testimony.

It is also the surviving fragment of something larger. 7343 is the truncated successor of sec. 1102 of the Senate-passed IAA division of S. 2226, which carried a contractor turn-in obligation, a list of non-earth-origin materials and a liability provision. None of that survived to enactment.
